newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kuehbacher - cap mkt convergence shows EMU optimism.
newsitem.headline: Kuehbacher - cap mkt convergence shows EMU optimism.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher said on Friday that the convergence of interest rates on European Union capital markets indicated markets were confident EMU would get off the ground.

"The reduction of differences in interest rates can be viewed as an indication that international financial markets are giving a currency union with some of the EU member states a high chance of realisation," Kuehbacher said.

In a speech delivered to a banking audience, Kuehbacher also repeated that the Bundesbank opposed any softening of the convergence criteria required to be part of Europe's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).

Kuehbacher acknowledged that the Maastricht Treaty left some leeway for interpretation at least on criteria on government debt and budget deficits, prompting political debate on a potentially more generous interpretation.

"I must give a clear refusal to such an attempt to start currency union at any price," he said, warning that worries about the solidity of the Euro could cause significant upheaval on financial markets and undermine the project's political credibility.
"A softening of the convergence criteria can thus not be viewed as one of the available options for economic and constitutional reasons," he said.

"If the currency union is to be a success, then the Euro must follow on to the deutsche mark's success on stability. From the very beginning, the Bundesbank has spoken out in favour of a narrow and strict...fulfilment of convergence criteria."
Kuehbacher, also president of the state central bank of Berlin and Brandenburg, was addressing a conference on the Euro. The text of his speech was made available in advance.
